alignments.note: Rule 50: relative and ἄν compressed into a single -soever word, so the pair is one aligned unit.
Modal auxiliary rides with the verb under rule 9, discontinuously under rule 15; head on the lexical verb under rule 17.
Rule 20: the genitive ὑμῶν is free and takes your, so the article realizes nothing.
Rule 86: supplied subordinator and subject on a participle are ordinary helpers; the preverb's forth rides inside the verb's own unit under rule 106, headed on the verb word.

Rules 42 and 101: the improper preposition keeps only the English phrase that renders the adverb itself. The ASV writes a determiner for the governed noun (that house), so the article anchors it and carries the case preposition of with it, leaving the adverb bare — as πέραν takes on the other side while the article takes of the. Corrected from out of, which left the preposition on the adverb while the article still took a determiner; rule 101 makes rule 21's determiner and nothing else the test.

Rule 60 with rule 76: the demonstrative ἐκείνης is already spent on the second that, so it is unavailable to displace this article, which takes the supplied demonstrative determiner with its case preposition riding along as in rules 21 and 60, headed on the determiner. Reading ἐκείνης as one discontinuous unit over both English that's, which would empty this article under rule 38 and leave out of whole on ἔξω under rule 101, remains defensible.
Rule 38: the demonstrative that occupies this phrase's determiner slot, so the article realizes nothing.
Attributive demonstrative standing with its own noun.
Rule 106: the preverb ἐκ- is realized by off inside the verb's own unit, headed on the verb word.
Case preposition rides with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause, discontinuously under rule 15.

review_notes: Corrected s013 and s014: the accepted alignment mixed the two branches of rules 42 and 101, keeping out of whole on the adverb while still handing the article a determiner. Rule 101 states that rule 21's determiner and nothing else moves the trailing preposition, so an article taking that takes of that with it, headed on that under rules 17 and 21, and the adverb is left bare.

The two English that's are distributed between s014 and s019 under rules 60 and 76 rather than joined on the demonstrative; the joined reading, which would empty both articles under rule 38 and restore out of whole to ἔξω, is named in the s013 and s014 notes.
Every other unit is unchanged; the partition still covers s001–s025 and t001–t028 exactly once across 24 units.
